audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict initial' (initial stress) rests on Emeneau 1944:16, a first-hand grammar sketch by the language's principal describer, and matches Gordon 2002 'Initial' and the StressTyp2 citation; nothing opened today (Subbaiah 1986, Rajasekaran 2008, LSI-TN 2023 Kota chapter) contradicts it — all are silent. But (a) we hold no file for the deciding passage: the verbatim quote exists only as snippet-stitched text from the earlier search and could not be re-verified today (HathiTrust/Google/IA/eScholarship all could not be reached by automated download), and (b) the one 344-pp reference grammar (Subbiah 1985) is unheld and unread. Hence 'thin' rather than at-risk: the source is authoritative for its era and the classification is typologically expected, but the quote is unconfirmable from disk. Action: obtain Emeneau 1944 pp.15-19 from HathiTrust via a browser (open full view) and save it, then populate the empty top-le
audit.second_reader_evidence: 1) The other first reader's readings of the held/downloaded files are correct and I re-verified them: Subbaiah 1986 Kota Phonetic Reader has only a generic definition of stress (sec. 1.4 'Stress', printed pp.34-35, lines 1635-1647) and the Kota-specific part (p.47 'All the roots in Kota have only one syllable..') says nothing about accent; Rajasekaran 2008 ch.2 'Phonology comparison of Kota and Tamil' (pp.24-101; is held by the project) has zero stress/accent hits; LSI-Tamil Nadu 2023 Kota chapter (Banerjee, pp.411-457) has phonology subsections 2.1-2.6 (inventory, distribution, diphthongs, allophones, clusters, syllable) and no suprasegmental section — only the generic line 'rhythm..
